chapter.title: Food and Health
chapter.tagline: Discovering balanced nutrition, the digestive system, seasonal farming, and traditional preservation
chapter.overview: Dr. Anita joins family grandparents to discuss the wisdom of the traditional Indian thali. Students learn about the major nutrient groups (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, roughage), explore how food moves through the digestive tract, and celebrate seasonal millets.

sections.title: The Balanced Thali: Nutrients Our Body Needs
sections.subtitle: Carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, and minerals

storyNarrative.dialogue: Look at this traditional thali: roti and rice give us energy (carbs); dal gives protein to grow muscles; green sabzi gives vitamins and minerals to fight illnesses!

concept.heading: Components of a Balanced Diet
concept.keyRule: A balanced diet provides all essential nutrients in the correct proportions along with dietary roughage and clean water.

sections.title: From Tasting to Digesting
sections.subtitle: How teeth, saliva, stomach acid, and intestines absorb nutrients

storyNarrative.dialogue: When I chew dry roti for a long time, it starts tasting sweet! Dadi says my saliva is already breaking down the food!

concept.heading: Salivary Digestion & Gastrointestinal Absorption
concept.keyRule: Salivary amylase begins breaking starches into simple sugars. The stomach and small intestine further break down and absorb nutrients into blood.

sections.title: Seasonal Agriculture: Millets and Grains
sections.subtitle: Why eating seasonal crops and ancient millets promotes climate and human health

storyNarrative.dialogue: In winter we eat Bajra (pearl millet) and sesame; in summer we drink chilled sattu! Traditional millets require very little water and enrich our soil!

concept.heading: Nutri-Cereals (Millets) and Seasonality
concept.keyRule: Millets (Ragi, Jowar, Bajra) are drought-resistant, iron-rich, high in fibre, and suited to local seasonal climates.

questions.prompt: Why are millets like Ragi and Jowar considered climate-resilient superfoods?
options: They need massive amounts of pesticide
They grow with very little water and are packed with minerals
They only grow in winter greenhouses
questions.correctAnswer: They grow with very little water and are packed with minerals
questions.hint: Millets thrive in dry conditions and have high nutritional density.

sections.title: Traditional Food Preservation Techniques
sections.subtitle: Pickling, sun-drying, salting, and preventing spoilage

storyNarrative.dialogue: When raw mangoes are abundant in summer, we slice them, rub with salt and turmeric, sun-dry them, and store in mustard oil to last all year!

concept.heading: Inhibiting Microbial Growth
concept.keyRule: Removing moisture (sun-drying) or creating high osmotic/acidic barriers (salt, sugar, vinegar, oil) prevents fungal and bacterial rot.

It makes them turn into sugar
